intent: DT-0009's ruling lands on the agent's own evaluation page: the signals-disagreed sentence takes the notice role.
rationale: The same sentence, the same meaning, the same page shape as the competitor's evaluation detail — 'Signals disagreed with each other on this candidate' says the aggregate below is a compromise between opposed readings, and here it matters more: this is the operator's own agent, and the disagreement is what the simulator section further down lets them interrogate. One ruling, both pages; leaving this one plain would make the two evaluation details disagree about how much disagreement matters.

design.layout: Unchanged — score line, conflict notice when present, cost, chain, conditions, attributions, simulator, scorecard.

conflict.content: The sentence takes the notice role: color.notice.subtle background, 1px color.notice.border border, radius.2, space.4 padding, color.text.primary. Copy verbatim — identical treatment to DT-0009 on explorer-evaluation.

acceptance: When signals disagreed, the sentence renders in a notice block identical to DT-0009's on the explorer evaluation page
When they did not, nothing renders and no space is reserved
Zero copy changes anywhere on the page
No raw color, spacing, or size literal is introduced

references.value: Backlog #108 gap 2, sixth surface pass. The stages page's per-card conflict lines stay in words, per DT-0009's per-card ruling.
